title: ～まい (〜mai)
shortExplanation: Express a negative conjecture or determination; 'probably not' or 'I will not'.
longExplanation: The ～まい grammar point is used to express a negative conjecture or a strong determination not to do something. In modern usage, it is generally used with the dictionary form of verbs (来る→来るまい, する→するまい, etc.). It can be translated as 'probably not' or 'I will not' in English.

examples.jp: こんなに遅れては、電車に間に合うまい。
examples.romaji: Konnani okurete wa, densha ni maniau mai.
examples.en: Being this late, I probably won't make it for the train.

examples.jp: あの人は絶対に忘れるまい。
examples.romaji: Ano hito wa zettai ni wasureru mai.
examples.en: That person will definitely not forget.

examples.jp: 私は二度とその失敗を繰り返すまい。
examples.romaji: Watashi wa nidoto sono shippai o kurikaesu mai.
examples.en: I will not repeat that mistake again.

usageNote: Formal, literary negative conjecture - "probably not/I won't" - the negative counterpart to だろう.
